title: Brown's work witnessed by top government and military figures

tellings.quote: One in which Townsen Brown isn't easily dismissed as an amateur quack. In fact, his work was witnessed by the highest levels of government and military.

plain: The work of an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown, whom Michels links to antigravity propulsion, was seen by people at the very top of government and the military, Michels says. He draws this from The Man Who Mastered Gravity, a book by Paul Schatzkin, and names such as the physicist Edward Teller and the aviation inventor Bill Lear come up in it. Michels tells it to argue that Brown cannot easily be dismissed as an amateur crank.
